sourcedFrom: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 (2018 or later (warranty effective 1 Jan 2018))
cleanIntro: The 590M is a 590 that feeds from a box, and that one change rewrites the first minute of every cleaning session: the magazine coming out proves nothing about the chamber. Mossberg's own interval is every 200 rounds. Strip is the familiar 590 sequence — cap, barrel, then two punches — with a magazine catch that comes out on its own pair of pins.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward, fingers off the trigger
steps.action: Push the safety button on the top rear of the receiver fully back to ON before you touch anything else, and keep the muzzle pointed somewhere harmless. For the whole unload your trigger finger stays outside the guard — you are about to run a loaded action deliberately.
steps.quote: Move the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position. During unloading, never allow fingers or any other objects to contact the trigger.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.9

steps.title: ⛔ The magazine out is NOT the gun empty — the chamber still holds one
steps.action: Press the magazine release on either side of the receiver, rotate the magazine forward and pull it clear. Then understand what you have and have not done: a 590M with the magazine on the bench will still fire the round in its chamber. This is the single most dangerous misreading a box-fed pump invites, and the book prints a warning about it on its own.
steps.aside: FIREARM WILL FIRE WITH MAGAZINE REMOVED.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by depressing the magazine release button on either the left or right side of the receiver, while grasping and rotating the magazine forward, pull it away from the firearm.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.9

steps.title: Action lock lever, then the forearm all the way back
steps.action: Depress the action lock lever on the left of the trigger housing and pull the forearm fully rearward. That extracts whatever was in the chamber without your finger going near the trigger, which is exactly why the lever exists.
steps.quote: Depress the action lock lever and pull the forearm fully rearward, this should extract a loaded shotshell from the chamber.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.9

steps.title: Look and feel — both, every time
steps.action: With the action open, put your eyes on the chamber and receiver and then put a finger in. Eyes alone miss a shell in bad light and a finger alone misses a shell you can see; the book asks for both and names all three places to check.
steps.quote: After unloading always visually and physically inspect the chamber, receiver and magazine to make sure that all of the shotshells have been removed.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.9

steps.title: Eye protection on before a single part moves
steps.action: Put glasses on now rather than when something pings across the bench. There are springs in this gun that leave under their own power, and the magazine you are about to set aside has one of them.
steps.quote: Always wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.10

steps.title: Bolt to mid-port — the position the cap comes off at
steps.action: From fully rearward, walk the forearm slowly forward until the front of the bolt sits in the middle of the ejection port. Fully forward or fully back both fight you on the next step; this is the position the barrel wants to be released at.
steps.quote: Move the forearm slowly forward from the fully rearward position until the front of the bolt is in the middle of the ejection port.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.10

steps.title: Magazine cap off the guide tube, counterclockwise
steps.action: Turn the magazine cap counterclockwise until its threads are completely off the guide tube. Fingers only. Note the word guide tube — on a 590M this is not a magazine tube full of shells, which is why there is no spring waiting behind the cap.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine cap by turning it counterclockwise until the cap threads are completely disengaged from the end of the guide tube
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.10

steps.title: Barrel out with a rocking pull, not a straight yank
steps.action: Work the barrel back and forth in small rotations while you draw it forward out of the receiver. The barrel extension is a close fit in the receiver; rotation breaks the friction that a straight pull just increases.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel with a gentle back-and-forth rotational movement while pulling the barrel out of the receiver assembly.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.10

steps.title: Magazine catch pins — 3/32" punch, no bigger
steps.action: Drive out the two magazine catch pins with a punch no larger than 3/32". Oversize punches swell the pin holes in an aluminium receiver and the catch never sits right again. Then rotate the catch away from the trigger guard and lift it out.
steps.quote: Using a small punch, no larger than 3/32”, push out the two magazine catch pins.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.10

steps.title: Trigger housing pin — 1/8" punch, then straight out
steps.action: Drive the trigger housing pin out with a punch no larger than 1/8" and pull the housing straight down out of the receiver. Straight is the operative word; levering it out bends the tabs that locate it.
steps.aside: The trigger housing assembly is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled.
steps.quote: Using a small punch, no larger than 1/8”, push out the trigger housing pin.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.10

steps.title: Bolt slide out through the clearance cut
steps.action: Run the forearm back until the bottom of the bolt slide lines up with the clearance cut in the receiver walls, then rotate the back of the slide up and lift it out. The cut is the only place the slide will pass; if it will not come, it is not aligned, and force will not align it.
steps.quote: Move the forearm/action slide assembly rearward so that the bottom of the bolt slide is aligned with the clearance cut in the sides of the receiver.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.11

steps.title: Bolt forward, nose down, out
steps.action: Slide the bolt to the front of the receiver, lift its back end and draw it out. It comes out at an angle because the ejector has to clear its slot on the way.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt assembly by sliding it forward to the front end of the receiver, lift the back end of the bolt up and pull it out of the receiver
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.11

steps.title: Forearm and action slide off the guide tube
steps.action: Slide the forearm assembly forward and off the front of the guide tube. That is the field strip finished — five groups on the bench and nothing else needs to come apart to clean this gun properly.
steps.quote: Remove the forearm/action slide assembly by sliding it forward and off the guide tube.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.11

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel, forearm and action slide, bolt, bolt slide, trigger housing and magazine catch. Mossberg draws the line here for routine work, and anything past it belongs to a Product Service Center.
steps.cite: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 103185 — DISASSEMBLY, p.11

deepAbsentReason: This book publishes one teardown and stops at the field strip, in its own words: the firearm should not be disassembled further for routine cleaning and maintenance, and further disassembly belongs to an authorized Product Service Center or a qualified gunsmith. ⛔ No deeper path is invented for it.

cleaning.name: BARREL — bore and chamber
tasks: Solvent on a brass brush through bore and chamber
Patches until they come out clean
One lightly oiled patch last, as a protective film
Brass bristles only for stubborn deposits — never steel
cleaning.quote: Scrub bore and chamber with solvent and follow with cleaning patches until barrel is clean.
cleaning.src: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual, BARREL CLEANING, p.12

cleaning.name: ACTION — bolt, bolt slide, action bars
tasks: Evaporating solvent on bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars
Get residue out of the bolt face and under the extractor
Lubricate sparingly — action parts stay clean longer dry than oily
cleaning.quote: Clean all components of the action including the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars to remove accumulated residue.
cleaning.src: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual, ACTION CLEANING, p.12

cleaning.name: RECEIVER — and the magazine well tracks
tasks: Rag or soft brush inside the receiver
Pay attention to the tracks the action bars run in
Wipe the magazine catch and its seat while the catch is out
Light oil on internal and external surfaces, then wipe back
cleaning.quote: Very little lubrication other than a light oiling of internal and external surfaces to prevent rusting is needed.
cleaning.src: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.12

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE — only if it needs it
tasks: 1/8" punch on the button in the bottom cover, keep a hand over it
Slide the cover off against spring pressure, then release slowly
Note which way the follower faces before anything leaves the body
Wipe the body dry — oil in a magazine collects grit and stops feed
cleaning.quote: To disassemble the magazine, use a 1/8” punch to depress and hold down the button located on the bottom cover of the magazine.
cleaning.src: 590M™ 12 GA. PUMP ACTION SHOTGUN WITH DETACHABLE MAGAZINE — Mossberg owner's manual, DISASSEMBLING THE MAGAZINE, p.12

reassembly: Safety still ON. Receiver on the bench, trigger housing opening upwards.
Forearm assembly onto the guide tube, action bars into their cuts in the receiver.
Bolt in at an angle, bolt lock down, front first, then rotate the back down.
Line the ejector up with the ejector slot as the bolt slides rearward.
Bolt slide in with the three-slotted side up and the notch to the rear, front lowered first.
Trigger housing in with the hammer FULLY COCKED, or it will not seat.
Trigger housing pin in flush. If it fights you, check the housing's own pins are flush first.
Magazine catch in at a slight angle, contoured side toward the trigger guard, then its two pins flush.
Barrel into the receiver, magazine cap FINGER TIGHT ONLY — no pliers, no wrench.
Look through the ejection port and confirm the barrel extension is seated against its shoulder before you call it assembled.
fncheck: Safety ON, muzzle safe, action open, and check the chamber, receiver and magazine well are empty. Hold the action lock lever and cycle the action several times for free movement. Close it, safety still ON, pull the trigger — the hammer must NOT fall. Finger off, move the safety to FIRE — the hammer must NOT fall on its own. Then pull the trigger and it should fall. Open the action and set the safety back to ON. Anything that does not behave exactly that way is a Product Service Center job, not a range problem.
